mainTopic: Which kings ruled the whole world, and how בלשצר and אחשורוש miscounted the seventy years of exile before the feast in the מגילה.
overview: On the previous amud, the גמרא said that three kings ruled the whole world, including אחשורוש. Here it tests that list against four more kings: שלמה, סנחריב, דריוש and כורש. Each is rejected. שלמה lost his throne for a time, or else his rule was greater than world rule. סנחריב never took ירושלים, דריוש ruled only 120 provinces, and כורש was just boasting. Then the גמרא turns to the next פסוק in the מגילה, which seems to place the feast both at the start of אחשורוש's reign and in his third year. רבא explains that 'כשבת' means once his mind was settled, after he counted the seventy years of ירמיה's prophecy and believed they had passed. The גמרא shows how בלשצר miscounted, used the vessels of the בית המקדש and was killed. It then shows how אחשורוש made his own count, made the same mistake, and was punished when ושתי was killed. It ends by showing that the correct count runs from the destruction of ירושלים. Because the years were partial years, the seventy years ended only in the second year of דריוש.

steps.title: Memory aid, then the question: what about שלמה?
steps.stepSummary: After a memory aid for the coming kings, the גמרא asks why שלמה is missing from the list of kings who ruled the whole world.
steps.simpleTranslation: (Memory aid: ש, ס, ד, כ.) Is there really no one else? But there is שלמה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a short memory aid for the kings it is about to discuss. Then it challenges the list of three world rulers by pointing to שלמה המלך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list said only three kings ruled the entire world. But everyone knows שלמה had a huge, famous kingdom. If he also ruled the world, the list of three is incomplete.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory aid, here the first letters of the kings about to be discussed

steps.confusionAlert: The סימן is not part of the argument. It just helps you remember the order: שלמה, סנחריב, דריוש, כורש.

phrases.english: (Memory aid: Shin, Samech, Dalet, Kaf)
phrases.notes: These letters stand for שלמה, סנחריב, דריוש and כורש, the kings the גמרא is about to discuss, in that order.

phrases.english: And is there no one else?
But there is Solomon!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier list of three world rulers, which comes on the previous amud
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that only three kings (אחאב, אחשורוש, נבוכדנצר) ruled the entire world
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שלמה also had a world-wide kingdom, so the list seems to be missing him

steps.title: שלמה's kingship was not complete
steps.stepSummary: שלמה is left off because his reign did not stay whole to the end.
steps.simpleTranslation: His kingship did not last to the end.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that שלמה does not count, because his reign did not continue all the way through his life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To be on the list, a king must hold world rule completely. שלמה lost his throne during his lifetime, so his rule was cut off. That is enough to keep him off the list.

keyTerms.meaning: Did not go up to the end; was not completed

phrases.english: His kingship did not complete itself.
phrases.notes: שלמה lost his throne during his lifetime, so his reign wasn't complete.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: the king's reign was not complete
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שלמה's great kingdom should put him on the list
steps.terutzMaskana: An interrupted reign does not count as full world rule

steps.title: That answer fails for the view that שלמה became king again
steps.stepSummary: The answer from step 2 works only for the view that שלמה never returned to the throne. What about the view that he returned?
steps.simpleTranslation: That works for the one who says he was a king and then a commoner. But for the one who says he was a king, then a commoner, then a king again, what can you say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks its own answer from step 2. There is a disagreement about whether שלמה ever got his throne back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If שלמה became a commoner and stayed one, his reign was truly broken. But one view says he became king again at the end. On that view his reign did reach completion, so step 2's answer no longer explains why he is left off the list.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who said
What can be said? (the answer seems to fail)

steps.confusionAlert: Both views agree שלמה lost his throne for a while. They argue only about whether he got it back at the end.

phrases.english: This works well for the one who says: a king and then a commoner.
But for the one who says
a king, then a commoner, then a king again —
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר מֶלֶךְ וְהֶדְיוֹט אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר מֶלֶךְ וְהֶדְיוֹט וּמֶלֶךְ מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 2
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that שלמה's kingship was incomplete
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to the view that שלמה returned to the throne, his reign was completed, so the answer does not work

steps.title: שלמה ruled even over the upper worlds
steps.stepSummary: שלמה's rule was a different kind altogether, because it covered the upper worlds as well as the earth. So he cannot be compared to the other kings.
steps.simpleTranslation: שלמה had something else about him: he ruled over the upper beings and the lower beings, as it says, 'And שלמה sat on the throne of ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer that works even for the view that שלמה returned to the throne.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list is of kings who ruled the whole earth. שלמה's rule went beyond that and reached the upper worlds too, which the פסוק hints at by calling his throne 'the throne of ה׳.' So he is not missing from the list. He belongs in a class of his own, above it.

keyTerms.meaning: The upper beings, in the heavenly worlds

steps.whatToRemember: שלמה is not on the list for one of two reasons. Either his reign was broken, or his rule was greater than world rule, since it reached the upper worlds too.

phrases.english: Solomon had something else about him —
that he ruled over the upper beings and over the lower beings,
as it says: 'And Solomon sat on the throne of the LORD.'
phrases.notes: This פסוק is in דברי הימים א׳ 29:23. Sitting on 'the throne of ה׳' shows his rule reached beyond the earth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 3
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: שלמה's rule was a different kind, greater than world rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If שלמה's reign was completed, he should be on the list
steps.terutzMaskana: שלמה is in a class of his own, ruling both the upper and lower worlds, so he cannot be counted with ordinary world rulers

steps.title: What about סנחריב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests סנחריב as a world ruler, based on his boast that no country's gods saved it from him.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there was סנחריב, as it is written: 'Who among all the gods of these lands saved their land from my hand?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new challenge to the list. סנחריב boasted that he conquered every land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: סנחריב's boast suggests that no country escaped him. If so, he ruled the whole world and should be on the list.

phrases.english: But there was Sennacherib, as it is written:
'Who among all the gods of these lands
phrases.notes: This is from ישעיהו 36:20. סנחריב's messenger is boasting to the people of ירושלים.

phrases.english: have saved their land from my hand?'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge to the same list, after the שלמה discussion ends
steps.kashyaTarget: The list of three world rulers
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: סנחריב's boast implies he conquered every land, so he should be on the list

steps.title: סנחריב never conquered ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: סנחריב does not count, because ירושלים stayed out of his hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is ירושלים, which he did not conquer!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that סנחריב did not rule the whole world, because he never captured ירושלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even one place left unconquered means the king did not rule everything. ירושלים was miraculously saved from סנחריב, so his rule was not complete.

phrases.english: But there is Jerusalem, which he did not conquer!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 5
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual limitation: one territory remained unconquered
steps.terutzHavaAmina: סנחריב's boast means he ruled everywhere
steps.terutzMaskana: ירושלים was not conquered, so סנחריב did not rule the whole world

steps.title: What about דריוש?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests דריוש, who wrote a letter to all peoples 'who dwell in all the earth.'
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is דריוש, as it is written: 'King דריוש wrote to all the peoples, nations and languages that dwell in all the earth: May your peace be great!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another king who seems to have ruled the whole world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דריוש addressed his letter to everyone living 'in all the earth.' That sounds as if his rule covered the entire world, so he should be on the list.

phrases.english: But there is Darius, as it is written:
'King Darius wrote
phrases.notes: This פסוק is from דניאל 6:26, which is written in Aramaic.

phrases.english: to all the peoples, nations and languages
who dwell in all the earth:
May your peace be great!'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge to the same list, after the סנחריב discussion ends
steps.kashyaTarget: The list of three world rulers
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: דריוש wrote to all who live 'in all the earth,' which implies he ruled the whole world

steps.title: דריוש ruled only 120 provinces
steps.stepSummary: דריוש does not count, because he set officials over just 120 provinces. That leaves seven he did not rule, compared to אחשורוש's 127.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are seven that he did not rule over, as it is written: 'It pleased דריוש to set over the kingdom 120 satraps.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that דריוש's kingdom was smaller than the whole world. It proves this from the number of officials he appointed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דריוש appointed officials over 120 provinces. אחשורוש, who is on the list, ruled 127, so seven provinces were outside דריוש's rule. His letter to 'all the earth' was a grand way of speaking, not a sign of true world rule.
steps.whatToRemember: A king counts as a world ruler only if nothing at all is left outside his rule. סנחריב missed ירושלים, and דריוש missed seven provinces.

phrases.aramaic: הָא אִיכָּא שְׁבַע דְּלָא מְלַךְ עֲלַיְיהוּ, דִּכְתִיב:
phrases.english: But there are seven he did not rule over, as it is written:
phrases.notes: Seven fewer than אחשורוש, who ruled 127 provinces according to the start of מגילת אסתר.

phrases.english: 'It pleased Darius
phrases.notes: This is from דניאל 6:2.

phrases.english: to set over the kingdom
one hundred and twenty satraps.'

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא אִיכָּא שְׁבַע דְּלָא מְלַךְ עֲלַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 7
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proof from a פסוק that the territory was limited
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The letter to 'all the earth' shows דריוש ruled the whole world
steps.terutzMaskana: דריוש ruled only 120 provinces, seven fewer than אחשורוש, so he was not a world ruler

steps.title: What about כורש, who said he got all the kingdoms?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests כורש as another king who ruled the whole world, based on his own words in עזרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is כורש! It is written: 'Thus says כורש, king of Persia: All the kingdoms of the earth the Lord has given me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers one more candidate for a king who ruled the whole world: כורש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא said only three kings ruled the whole world, and it has been rejecting other candidates one by one. כורש seems to fit, because a פסוק quotes him saying God gave him 'all the kingdoms of the earth.' If he counts, the list of world rulers would be wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: כורש, the king of Persia who allowed the Jews to return

phrases.english: But there is Cyrus,
as it is written: "Thus says Cyrus, king of Persia:
phrases.notes: This פסוק is from the very start of ספר עזרא.

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל מַמְלְכוֹת הָאָרֶץ נָתַן לִי ה׳״!
phrases.english: All the kingdoms of the earth the Lord has given me"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge to the same list, after the דריוש discussion ends.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that only a few kings, אחשורוש among them, ruled the whole world.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק quotes כורש saying he received all the kingdoms of the earth, so he looks like a world ruler too.

steps.title: כורש was just boasting
steps.stepSummary: כורש's words are not proof, because he was only bragging about himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: There he was simply boasting about himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects כורש as a world ruler. His statement was bragging, not a fact.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק does say these words, but it is only quoting what כורש said about himself. A boast does not show what he actually ruled. So the list of world rulers stays as it was.
steps.whatToRemember: Every proposed world ruler (סנחריב, דריוש, כורש) has been rejected, so אחשורוש stays on the short list of kings who ruled the whole world.

phrases.english: There, it is boasting
that he is boasting about himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם אִשְׁתַּבּוֹחֵי הוּא דְּקָא מִשְׁתַּבַּח בְּנַפְשֵׁיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from כורש.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the source: it shows what he claimed, not what was true.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a פסוק says כורש received all the kingdoms, he must have ruled the whole world.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק only records his bragging, so it proves nothing about his real power.

steps.title: Was the feast in the king's first year or his third?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out two פסוקים next to each other that seem to give different times for the feast.
steps.simpleTranslation: It says 'In those days, when the king sat,' and right after it says 'In the third year of his reign'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next פסוק in the מגילה and points out an apparent contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'When the king sat' on his throne sounds like the very start of his reign. But the next פסוק says the feast was in his third year. Which one is right?

keyTerms.meaning: when the king sat (on his throne)

steps.confusionAlert: This is a new topic. The 'world ruler' discussion is finished, and the גמרא is now going through the next פסוקים of the מגילה.

phrases.english: "In those days, when the king sat,"
phrases.notes: This is אסתר 1:2. 'Sat' makes it sound like he had just taken the throne.

phrases.english: and it is written right after it:
"In the third year of his reign"!

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּיָּמִים הָהֵם כְּשֶׁבֶת הַמֶּלֶךְ וּכְתִיב בָּתְרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the world-ruler discussion and starts on the next פסוק of the מגילה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The simple reading of 'כשבת המלך' as the start of the reign.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'sat' means his first year, it clashes with the next פסוק, which says the third year.

steps.title: רבא: 'sat' means after his mind was settled
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that 'כשבת' means once the king's mind was at ease. He believed he could count correctly where בלשצר had failed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: What does 'when he sat' mean? After his mind was settled. He said: בלשצר calculated and made a mistake. I will calculate and I will not make a mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the contradiction. 'Sat' does not mean when he took the throne. It means when he calmed down, which happened in his third year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא reads 'כשבת' as coming from the word for being settled (נתיישבה). Something was bothering אחשורוש, and only in year three did he feel secure enough to throw the feast. What bothered him was a calculation that בלשצר had already gotten wrong, and the גמרא is about to explain it.

keyTerms.meaning: his mind became settled, he calmed down

steps.confusionAlert: רבא does not drop the word 'sat.' He shows it means 'settled in his mind,' so both פסוקים point to the third year.

phrases.english: Rava said:
What is the meaning of "when he sat"?
After his mind was settled.
phrases.notes: 'כשבת' (sitting) and 'נתיישבה' (settled) come from the same root, ישב.

phrases.english: He said: Belshazzar calculated and erred,
phrases.notes: 'He said' means אחשורוש said this to himself.

phrases.english: I will calculate and I will not err.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the contradiction by explaining what the word 'כשבת' really means.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets a word: 'sat' means 'settled in mind,' not 'took the throne.'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'כשבת' means the start of his reign, which clashes with 'the third year.'
steps.terutzMaskana: 'כשבת' means after he calmed down, which was in the third year, so the פסוקים agree.

steps.title: What was the calculation? The seventy-year prophecy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what calculation is meant and brings the two פסוקים that promise redemption after seventy years.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is this calculation? It is written: 'After seventy years are completed for Babylonia, I will remember you,' and it is written: 'To complete seventy years for the ruins of ירושלים.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining the calculation. First it quotes the prophecies about the seventy years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ירמיה promised the Jews would be redeemed after seventy years. The kings of Babylonia and Persia were nervous about this and tried to work out when the seventy years would end. Two פסוקים describe the seventy years: one counts 'for Babylonia' and one counts 'for the ruins of Jerusalem.'

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? (asks for an explanation)

phrases.english: What is it? —
As it is written: "For after the completion for Babylonia
phrases.notes: This is ירמיה 29:10.

phrases.english: of seventy years, I will remember you,"
and it is written: "To complete for the ruins of Jerusalem
phrases.notes: This is דניאל 9:2. Notice it counts from Jerusalem's ruins, while the first פסוק counts for Babylonia.

phrases.english: seventy years."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the calculation that רבא mentioned.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What calculation did בלשצר make and get wrong?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It was a count of the seventy years promised in ירמיה and דניאל before the redemption.

steps.title: Belshazzar's count and his use of the Temple vessels
steps.stepSummary: בלשצר added 45 years of נבוכדנצר, 23 of אויל מרודך, and 2 of his own to reach seventy. Thinking the promise had failed, he used the vessels of the בית המקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: He counted: forty-five years of נבוכדנצר, twenty-three of אויל מרודך, and two of his own — that makes seventy. He took out the vessels of the בית המקדש and used them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows exactly how בלשצר counted and what he did once he thought the seventy years were over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בלשצר counted from the start of נבוכדנצר's reign and reached seventy years with no redemption. He concluded the prophecy had failed and dared to use the holy vessels. אחשורוש's words in step 12, 'בלשצר calculated and erred,' already tell us this count was wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: the vessels of the בית המקדש

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up why אחשורוש waited until his third year. He wanted to fix בלשצר's mistake before celebrating, and that explains the contradiction in the פסוקים.

phrases.english: He calculated: forty-five of Nebuchadnezzar,
phrases.notes: 'He' is בלשצר, and the numbers are years each king reigned.

phrases.english: and twenty-three of Evil-merodach,
and two of his own — that makes seventy.
He took out the vessels of the Temple
and used them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes explaining the calculation by showing בלשצר's actual count and what he did next.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 45 + 23 + 2 = 70 years with no redemption, so בלשצר thought the promise had failed and used the holy vessels.

steps.title: How do we know נבוכדנצר reigned forty-five years?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that נבוכדנצר ruled for forty-five years.
steps.simpleTranslation: And נבוכדנצר — from where do we know that he reigned forty-five years?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to check one number in בלשצר's count: the forty-five years of נבוכדנצר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole seventy-year total depends on each king's number. The 45 years of נבוכדנצר is not stated outright in one פסוק, so the גמרא asks for proof. This question sets up the proof that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: נבוכדנצר, king of Babylonia who destroyed the first בית המקדש

phrases.english: And Nebuchadnezzar, from where do we know
that he reigned forty-five years?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּנְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר מְנָלַן דְּאַרְבְּעִין וַחֲמֵשׁ שְׁנִין מְלַךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the first number in בלשצר's count.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that נבוכדנצר reigned forty-five years.

steps.title: Two exiles, each given two dates
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts its proof by quoting a teaching: the Jews were exiled in the seventh, eighth, eighteenth, and nineteenth years.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Master said: They were exiled in the seventh year, they were exiled in the eighth, they were exiled in the eighteenth, they were exiled in the nineteenth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins answering by quoting a known teaching about the dates of the exiles. It will use these dates to build up the forty-five years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teaching gives four numbers, but they describe only two exiles. Each exile is dated twice: once from נבוכדנצר's conquest of יהויקים and once from the start of נבוכדנצר's reign. The next step explains this, and the proof continues from there.

keyTerms.meaning: as the Master said (quoting an earlier teaching)

steps.confusionAlert: The answer is not finished here. These four dates are only the first piece of the proof.

phrases.english: As the Master said:
They were exiled in the seventh, they were exiled in the eighth,

phrases.aramaic: גָּלוּ בִּשְׁמוֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה, גָּלוּ בִּתְשַׁע עֶשְׂרֵה.
phrases.english: they were exiled in the eighteenth, they were exiled in the nineteenth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question about נבוכדנצר's forty-five years.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The start of the proof: a teaching giving the dates seventh, eighth, eighteenth, and nineteenth. These are two exiles, each counted two ways.

steps.title: Matching the exile years to נבוכדנצר's reign
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the ברייתא. The 7th year after the conquest of יהויקים, the exile of יהויכין, was the 8th year of נבוכדנצר. The 18th year, the exile of צדקיהו, was his 19th year.
steps.simpleTranslation: They were exiled in the seventh year after the conquest of יהויקים. That was the exile of יהויכין, which was the eighth year of נבוכדנצר's reign. They were exiled in the eighteenth year after the conquest of יהויקים. That was the exile of צדקיהו, which was the nineteenth year of נבוכדנצר's reign.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the four numbers from the ברייתא in Step 16. Each exile has two numbers: one counted from the conquest of יהויקים, and one counted from the start of נבוכדנצר's reign.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two ways of counting are always one year apart. The 7th year of one count is the 8th year of the other, and the 18th is the 19th. This tells us that יהויכין was exiled in נבוכדנצר's 8th year, which the proof will need soon.

keyTerms.meaning: The conquest of יהויקים by נבוכדנצר, one starting point for counting
The exile of King יהויכין, the first of the two exiles
The exile of King צדקיהו, the later exile when the בית המקדש was destroyed

steps.confusionAlert: There are two ways of counting here. One counts from the conquest of יהויקים, and the other counts from the start of נבוכדנצר's reign. They are always one year apart, so '7' and '8' describe the same year.

phrases.english: They were exiled in the seventh
year after the conquest of Jehoiakim
the exile of Jehoiachin,
which is the eighth year of Nebuchadnezzar.
They were exiled in the eighteenth
year after the conquest of Jehoiakim
the exile of Zedekiah
which is the nineteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the four numbers of the ברייתא quoted in Step 16
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The exile of יהויכין was in נבוכדנצר's 8th year, and the exile of צדקיהו was in his 19th year

steps.title: Why the two counts are one year apart
steps.stepSummary: A teaching says נבוכדנצר conquered נינוה in his first year and יהויקים in his second year.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Master said: in his first year נבוכדנצר conquered נינוה, and in his second year he conquered יהויקים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to explain why the two counts in Step 17 are one year apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נבוכדנצר's reign started a full year before he conquered יהויקים. So 'year 7 after the conquest' is the same as 'year 8 of his reign.'

keyTerms.meaning: As the Master said; introduces a known teaching
נינוה, the city נבוכדנצר conquered in his first year

phrases.english: As the Master said:
In the first year he conquered Nineveh;
in the second, he conquered Jehoiakim.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר מָר שָׁנָה רִאשׁוֹנָה כִּיבֵּשׁ נִינְוֵה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the one-year gap used in Step 17
steps.raayaObject: That the conquest of יהויקים was in נבוכדנצר's second year
steps.raayaSupportSource: A teaching quoted with דאמר מר

steps.title: The פסוק about אויל מרודך freeing יהויכין
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says that in the 37th year of יהויכין's exile, אויל מרודך, in the first year of his reign, released יהויכין from prison.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is written: 'In the thirty-seventh year of the exile of יהויכין king of יהודה, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-fifth of the month, אויל מרודך king of Babylon, in the year he became king, lifted up the head of יהויכין king of יהודה and brought him out of prison.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק showing how long יהויכין sat in prison until נבוכדנצר died. This is the second piece of the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אויל מרודך freed יהויכין in his very first year as king. That means נבוכדנצר's reign ended in the 37th year of יהויכין's exile, so נבוכדנצר ruled during all 37 of those years.

keyTerms.meaning: אויל מרודך, the son and successor of נבוכדנצר
Lifted up the head; raised him up and showed him favor

phrases.english: And it is written: "And it came to pass in the thirty-seventh year
of the exile of Jehoiachin, king of Judea,
in the twelfth month,
on the twenty-fifth of the month,
Evil-merodach, king of Babylonia, lifted up
[in the year of his reign]
phrases.notes: This means his very first year as king, which is the key to the whole calculation.

phrases.english: the head of Jehoiachin, king of Judea,
and brought him out of prison."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the second piece of the proof: 37 years from יהויכין's exile until נבוכדנצר's death
steps.raayaObject: נבוכדנצר ruled 37 more years after the exile of יהויכין

steps.title: 8 plus 37 equals 45 years
steps.stepSummary: Eight years before the exile of יהויכין plus 37 years after it gives 45 years of נבוכדנצר's reign.
steps.simpleTranslation: Eight and thirty-seven make forty-five years of נבוכדנצר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds the numbers together and answers the question from Step 15.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From Step 17: יהויכין was exiled in נבוכדנצר's 8th year. From Step 19: נבוכדנצר ruled 37 more years after that. So 8 + 37 = 45, and that is the source for his 45 years.
steps.whatToRemember: נבוכדנצר's 45 years = 8 years until the exile of יהויכין + 37 years that יהויכין sat in prison.

phrases.english: Eight, and thirty-seven —
this makes forty-five of Nebuchadnezzar.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּמְנֵי וּתְלָתִין וּשְׁבַע הֲרֵי אַרְבְּעִין וַחֲמֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Combines Steps 17 and 19 to answer Step 15

steps.title: Completing בלשצר's seventy and his reaction
steps.stepSummary: There are 23 years of אויל מרודך, known by tradition, and 2 of בלשצר, which make seventy. בלשצר decided the Jews would never be redeemed and used the vessels of the בית המקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: The twenty-three years of אויל מרודך are known by tradition. With his own two years, that makes seventy. He said: 'Now they will certainly never be redeemed.' He took out the vessels of the בית המקדש and used them.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the 45 years are proven, the גמרא returns to finish the count from Step 14 and repeats what בלשצר did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no פסוק for אויל מרודך's 23 years; it is a received tradition. 45 + 23 + 2 = 70. בלשצר saw seventy years end with no redemption, so he thought נבואה had failed.

keyTerms.meaning: Here it means a received tradition, not a proof from a פסוק
The vessels of the בית המקדש

steps.confusionAlert: Here the word גמרא does not mean the Talmud. It means a tradition that was handed down.

phrases.english: And the twenty-three of Evil-merodach — by tradition,
and two of his own — that makes seventy.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר: הַשְׁתָּא וַדַּאי תּוּ לָא מִיפַּרְקִי,
phrases.english: He said: Now certainly they will no longer be redeemed,

phrases.aramaic: אַפֵּיק מָאנֵי דְּבֵי מַקְדְּשָׁא וְאִשְׁתַּמַּשׁ בְּהוּ.
phrases.english: he took out the vessels of the Temple and used them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the count of Step 14 now that the 45 years are proven
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: 45 + 23 + 2 = 70, so בלשצר thought the promise had failed and used the holy vessels

steps.title: דניאל's rebuke and בלשצר's death
steps.stepSummary: The פסוקים show that דניאל rebuked בלשצר for using the vessels, and that בלשצר was killed that same night.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what דניאל told him: 'You have lifted yourself up against the Lord of heaven, and they brought the vessels of His House before you.' And it is written: 'In that night בלשצר the Chaldean king was killed.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings פסוקים from ספר דניאל that match the story: בלשצר used the vessels and was punished right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק confirms that the vessels were the sin. The second shows the punishment came that very night. This proves that his count was wrong, because the Jews were not given up on.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what is meant when it says

phrases.english: This is what Daniel said to him:
"But you have lifted yourself up against the Lord of heaven;
and they have brought the vessels of His House before you,"
and it is written: "In that night
Belshazzar, the [Chaldean] king, was slain."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows from פסוקים that בלשצר's act was a sin and was punished
steps.raayaObject: בלשצר used the holy vessels and was killed for it

steps.title: דריוש takes over the kingdom
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says דריוש the Mede received the kingdom at about age 62.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is written: 'And דריוש the Mede received the kingdom, being about sixty-two years old.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא moves the story forward to the next kings, which leads to אחשורוש's own count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After בלשצר dies, rule passes to דריוש, and later to כורש and אחשורוש. These kings will soon be counted as part of אחשורוש's seventy years.

keyTerms.meaning: דריוש the Mede, the king after בלשצר

phrases.english: And it is written: "And Darius the Mede received the kingdom,
being about sixty-two years old."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves the timeline from בלשצר's death to the next king

steps.title: אחשורוש claims he will count correctly
steps.stepSummary: אחשורוש says בלשצר made a mistake, but he himself will count without making one.
steps.simpleTranslation: He (אחשורוש) said: 'He (בלשצר) made a mistake. I will calculate and not make a mistake.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to אחשורוש, who believes he can find where בלשצר went wrong. This sets up his new count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects back to Step 12, where רבא said אחשורוש's mind was 'settled' because he was sure of his count. Now we hear his reasoning.

phrases.english: He said: He erred,
phrases.notes: The speaker is אחשורוש, and 'he' is בלשצר.

phrases.english: I will calculate and not err.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to אחשורוש from Step 12 after finishing בלשצר's story
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אחשורוש believes בלשצר counted from the wrong starting point

steps.title: Seventy years for the exile, not the kingdom
steps.stepSummary: אחשורוש reads the פסוק 'seventy years for Babylon' as counting from the exile, not from the start of the Babylonian kingdom.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does it say 'for the kingdom of Babylon'? It says 'for Babylon.' What does 'for Babylon' mean? For the exile to Babylon.
steps.whatsHappening: אחשורוש explains what he thinks בלשצר's mistake was. The seventy years should start from the exile, not from נבוכדנצר's rise to power.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בלשצר started counting from the first year of נבוכדנצר's reign. אחשורוש says the פסוק's wording means the count starts from the exile of יהויכין. That moves the starting point later.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it written? (meaning: it is not written that way)

phrases.english: Is it written "for the kingdom of Babylonia"?
"For Babylonia" is written,
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק from Step 13: 'when seventy years are completed for Babylon.'

phrases.english: What is "for Babylonia"? For the exile of Babylonia.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives אחשורוש's reason why בלשצר was wrong
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Count seventy years from the start of נבוכדנצר's reign
steps.terutzMaskana: Count seventy years from the exile of יהויכין

steps.title: Making up the missing eight years
steps.stepSummary: Counting from the exile leaves eight years missing. אחשורוש fills them with 1 year of בלשצר, 5 of דריוש and כורש, and 2 of his own, which makes seventy.
steps.simpleTranslation: How many years are missing? Eight. He calculated and put in their place one year of בלשצר, five years of דריוש and כורש, and two years of his own. That makes seventy.
steps.whatsHappening: אחשורוש does the new math based on his reading of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Starting from the exile removes the 8 years before יהויכין was exiled, so 8 years must be added at the end. 1 + 5 + 2 = 8, so by his count the seventy years ended in his own time.

phrases.english: How many are lacking? Eight,
phrases.notes: These are the 8 years of נבוכדנצר before the exile of יהויכין, which no longer count.

phrases.english: he calculated and inserted in their place
one of Belshazzar,
and five of Darius and Cyrus,
and two of his own — that makes seventy.
phrases.notes: This time 'his own' means אחשורוש's years.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the new starting point from Step 25 to the actual count
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 8 missing years are made up by 1 (בלשצר) + 5 (דריוש and כורש) + 2 (אחשורוש)

steps.title: אחשורוש also uses the vessels
steps.stepSummary: When אחשורוש saw seventy years pass with no redemption, he decided they would never be redeemed and used the vessels of the בית המקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he saw that seventy years were complete and they were not redeemed, he said: 'Now they will certainly never be redeemed.' He took out the vessels of the בית המקדש and used them.
steps.whatsHappening: אחשורוש reaches the same wrong conclusion as בלשצר and repeats his sin. The גמרא uses the same words on purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The repeated wording shows the pattern: both kings counted, saw no redemption, and used the holy vessels. This explains the feast in מגילת אסתר.

phrases.english: Once he saw that seventy were completed
and they were not redeemed —

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר: הַשְׁתָּא וַדַּאי תּוּ לָא מִיפַּרְקִי,
phrases.english: he said: Now certainly they will no longer be redeemed,

phrases.aramaic: אַפֵּיק מָאנֵי דְּבֵי מַקְדְּשָׁא וְאִשְׁתַּמַּשׁ בְּהוּ.
phrases.english: he took out the vessels of the Temple and used them.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּחָזֵי דִּמְלוֹ שִׁבְעִין וְלָא אִיפְּרוּק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws אחשורוש's conclusion from his count in Step 26
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: אחשורוש thought the seventy years were over and used the holy vessels at his feast

steps.title: The punishment: ושתי is killed
steps.stepSummary: Because of this, the שטן came and danced among them, and אחשורוש killed ושתי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The שטן came and danced among them, and he killed ושתי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells the punishment for using the vessels. The party fell apart, and ושתי was killed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like בלשצר, אחשורוש was punished right away. The death of ושתי is what makes room for אסתר to become queen.

keyTerms.meaning: The שטן, the accusing force that causes trouble
Danced among them; stirred up confusion

steps.whatToRemember: Two kings made the same mistake about the seventy years. Each thought the redemption had failed and used the vessels of the בית המקדש, and each was punished: בלשצר was killed, and at אחשורוש's feast ושתי was killed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the story of the מגילה begins with the feast: using the holy vessels led to the death of ושתי, which set up אסתר's rise.

phrases.english: The Satan came and danced among them
and he killed Vashti.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the result of אחשורוש's sin in Step 27
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Using the holy vessels led to chaos at the feast and the death of ושתי

steps.title: But he counted correctly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the story: if אחשורוש counted the seventy years correctly, why was he wrong and punished?
steps.simpleTranslation: But he counted properly! (So why did this happen to him?)
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the story. אחשורוש seemed to fix בלשצר's mistake, so why was his conclusion still wrong?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In steps 25-26, אחשורוש counted from the exile and added up the missing eight years exactly. If that math was right, his conclusion that the Jews would never be redeemed should have been right too. The גמרא wants to know where the flaw is.

phrases.english: But he calculated properly?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the story told in steps 26-28: if his count was right, his conclusion should have been right too.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that אחשורוש was wrong to decide there would be no redemption.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His count of seventy years from the exile seemed correct, so his conclusion should have been correct.

steps.title: He should have counted from the destruction of ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: אחשורוש also made a mistake. The seventy years should start from the חורבן of ירושלים, not from the first exile.
steps.simpleTranslation: He too made a mistake, because he should have counted from the destruction of ירושלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that אחשורוש's count was wrong too. He started counting from the wrong event.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אחשורוש started from the first exile, the exile of יהויכין. The correct starting point is the destruction of ירושלים, which came later, in the days of צדקיהו. So his seventy years ended too early.

phrases.english: He too made a mistake,
for he should have counted from the destruction of Jerusalem.
phrases.notes: This means the destruction in the days of צדקיהו, not the earlier exile of יהויכין that אחשורוש used.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 29 by finding the flaw in אחשורוש's count.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies the wrong starting point for the count
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אחשורוש's count from the exile was correct.
steps.terutzMaskana: The seventy years must be counted from the destruction of ירושלים, so he ended his count too early.

steps.title: Then the בית המקדש should have been built in his fourteenth year
steps.stepSummary: There are eleven more years to count, and אחשורוש ruled for fourteen. So the בית המקדש should have been built in his fourteenth year. But a פסוק says the building stopped during his time.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end, how many years were missing? Eleven. How long did he rule? Fourteen. So in his fourteenth year the בית המקדש should have been built. Why then is it written: 'Then the work of the House of God in ירושלים stopped'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא does the math with the new starting point and finds a problem. Then it brings a פסוק that seems to clash with that math.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Counting from the destruction adds eleven years. Since אחשורוש ruled fourteen years, the seventy years should have ended during his reign, and the בית המקדש should have been built in his fourteenth year. But the פסוק in עזרא says the work stopped, and stayed stopped until the second year of דריוש.

phrases.english: In the end, how many were missing? Eleven.
How many years did he reign? Fourteen,
so in his own fourteenth year
the Temple should have been built,
why then is it written:
"Then the work stopped
on the House of God which is in Jerusalem"?
phrases.notes: This פסוק is from עזרא and goes on to say the work stayed stopped until the second year of דריוש.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the corrected starting point from step 30 and shows it creates a new problem with a פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The corrected count from the destruction of ירושלים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With eleven extra years inside a fourteen-year reign, the seventy years end in אחשורוש's time. But the פסוק says the building stopped, not that it was built.

steps.title: רבא: the years were partial years
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that some of the years counted were only partial years, so the full seventy were not finished until later.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: They were partial years.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge. The years in the count were not all full years, so the real total ran out later than it looked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some years were counted as whole years even though they were only parts of years. Once you look at the real time that passed, the seventy years were not complete in אחשורוש's fourteenth year. That is why the building stayed stopped until the second year of דריוש, just as the פסוק says.
steps.whatToRemember: אחשורוש's mistake was starting the count from the first exile instead of the destruction of ירושלים. Even the corrected count seems to end in his fourteenth year, but רבא explains that some years were only partial years, so the seventy years really ended only in the second year of דריוש.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבא is changing the number seventy. The promise is still seventy years. He is only saying some counted years were not full years, so the real seventy finished later.

phrases.english: Rava said:
They were partial years.
phrases.notes: Some years were counted as full even though only part of each year had passed, so the real seventy years ended later.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the פסוק in step 31.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Corrects how the years are counted
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every year in the count was a full year, so seventy years ended in אחשורוש's fourteenth year.
steps.terutzMaskana: The years were partial, so the full seventy ended only in the second year of דריוש, matching the פסוק.
